liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Stander On The Mountain** (3 reviews): Reviewer finds this version magical, especially for fans of Bruce; Reviewer ranks this the best Dead version of the song [13][15][17]
- **Victim Or The Crime** (2 reviews): Strange effects and an evil roaring sound run through it; the jam out leads into a joyful Eyes; Phil used a cow-mooing effect here, which reviewer says he never used on Victim at any other time [15][19]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Reviewer counts this among the best Candymans ever [20]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Reviewer finds this a bit of a mess, though the show is very good [23]
- **The Other One** (1 other source): The Other One space segment is included within The Other One track [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **Stander On The Mountain**: rare: 4 archived performances [25]
- **Beam**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [25]

## The recordings

- **gd90-10-28.sbd.jamphan.3264.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 165 min; rated 3.92/5 by 26 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard remarkably crisp; Reviewer hears muddy vocals, with Jerry's voice weakened and lyrics half-spoken [15][22]
- **gd1990-10-28.nak300.houck-wright.gmb.90833.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 163 min [5]
- **gd1990-10-28.167634.nak700.blend.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 163 min [6]
- **gd1990-10-28.nak300.andrewf.83696.sbeok.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 161 min [9]. Said about its sound: Taped from a balcony close to the stage, so the sound is decent; Loud distortion appears during Space [9]

## Around the show

- Bruce sat in and added to the band's sound; reviewer recalls piano and accordion parts [16]
- The show came while the Dead world mourned Brent's death; Bruce helped the music through it [17]
- Bruce joined at a time the band needed him, after Mydland's death [19]
- This Europe run sounds mellower, a West Coast feel, quite unlike the band four months earlier [17]
- The 10/22/90 show also has a nice, weird Victim [19]
- Reviewer considers this one of the last great Dead shows [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd90-10-28.sbd.jamphan.3264.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> DATx3 [1]. Also: Soundboard recording copied to DAT three times, then converted through Sony M-1, Midiman optical, SB Platinum, CoolEdit and CDWav to SHN; The SHN files were produced by JamPhan [1]
- **gd1990-10-28.nak300.houck-wright.gmb.90833.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Alf Houck and Robert Wright; transferred by Bill Koucky; source: Audience Master Cassette Nakamichi 300's Shotguns > Marantz PMD-430 w/Dolby B [5]. Also: Tape flips had no patch source; crossfades were applied after Maggie's Farm and during Space [5]
- **gd1990-10-28.167634.nak700.blend.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics x3 > unknown mixer > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [6]. Also: A Neumann RSM 190i-S source from Dan Liff and Doug Lamarre supplies a seven-second patch in Space [6]
- **gd1990-10-28.nak300.andrewf.83696.sbeok.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > Sony TC-D5M > MAC [9]. Also: A tape flip falls about 3:55 into Space and was mended together [9]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Zenith - October 28, 1990](https://www.dead.net/show/october-28-1990) [26]
- Fan art by Lyrics On Demand: [Grateful Dead Lyrics](https://www.lyricsondemand.com/grateful_dead) [27]
